basics.name: Lynne J. Xu
basics.label: Ph.D. Candidate, Environmental Sciences
basics.summary: Ph.D. candidate at the University of California, Riverside studying Southern California air quality. My research uses atmospheric chemical transport and dispersion models (WRF-Chem, AERMOD, WRF-STILT) together with observational data to examine wildfire plume transport and dispersion, transportation-related emissions, and their impacts on nearby communities.

highlights: Created hypothetical scenarios of identical fire conditions with different dates and corresponding meteorological conditions to analyze differences in the movement and dispersion of wildfire plumes. Built statistical models to predict wildfire plume dispersion and exposure of nearby residents.
Integrated computer-modeled transportation-related emissions into an atmospheric chemical transport model and analyzed the impact of the modeled emissions.
Analyzed observational air quality data to examine the relative impact of local and long-range transport emissions, supporting conclusions with modeled results.
